parts.transcript: Section 1: brother Rob and sister Margaret plan their father's 80th birthday party. Three hotels: Royal, Star, Winchester. Online booking only at Star (example=B). Sea view: Star out over the bay/cliff top (1=B). Disabled access: Winchester fine, Star fine, Royal had ramps installed recently - all three (2=D). Indoor play area: Royal none, Winchester has one on ground floor, Star's isn't under cover (3=C Winchester). Choice of food: Royal only one with a choice, others set menu (4=A). Private dining/own room: only Royal can provide (5=A). Group discount/reduction: Winchester offering a good reduction for the numbers (6=C). To do immediately: send a deposit (7) to secure booking; make the invitations (8) on computer. Later: find out who needs help with transport (9); tell people not to bring any presents (10).

parts.transcript: Section 2: director of the Montreal Curling Club. Four players: the lead (11), the second, the third and the skip. Area of play on the ice = the sheet (12). Target zones each known as a house (13). Stones from granite; brushes Scottish (horse hair, 14) vs Canadian (synthetic). Beginner needs a rubber (15) sole on one shoe. Captain carries a stopwatch (16). Montreal CC renowned as the first club for any sport in North America = oldest (17=B). Caledonian Curling Club set up to create standard rules (18=C). In the 16th century Scottish Parliament banned golf/football but not curling - throwing stones useful like shooting arrows = good training for battle (19=B). In Canada, granite hard to import so cast iron from melted cannon balls used (20=C).

parts.transcript: Section 3: students Josh and Emily on scientific techniques in art. Josh on Jackson Pollock: people think a child could paint one but they're incredibly intricate = complex (21=B). A $5 painting alleged genuine Pollock; strongest argument against = no records of previous owners = lacked documentation (22=A). International Foundation for Art Research worried about the acrylic paint used (unusual in Pollock's day) = type of paint (23=B). They agree they need a combination of art and science (24=C). Seracini's hunt for Da Vinci's Battle of Anghiari in the Hall of the 500, Florence: laser scanner to make a 3D model (25=D); thermographic camera to reveal materials/original architecture (26=G); space on east wall that held glass windows (27=F); radar to analyse the wall, found a second wall (28=E); painting believed on the original stone wall behind newer brick (29=C); now using a gamma-ray camera/technology to prove it (30=B).

parts.title: Sustainability
parts.transcript: Section 4: lecture on sustainability. Term first coined 1987 in a UN report. Lecture aim: analyse the confusion (31) surrounding sustainability. Sustainable development = meeting needs of present and future generations (32). Myth 1: original definition makes no mention of the environment (33); original focus was giving poorer nations the same rights (34) to natural resources as richer nations, to improve their living (35) standards/conditions. Myth 2: green vs sustainable; the lobby's key problem is time (36) to develop technology; the sustainability lobby is prepared to accept (37) nuclear energy unlike most greens. Myth 3: role of technology; battery stations on roads (38) = new business thinking not new tech; farmers plant sunflowers/wheat instead of corn (39) to save water; greater water use results from changes in our diet (40).
